 Falling Back: Trojans react to time change 
 Campus News Local News  | November 17, 2026 
 https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=fbA6J7n_VNA&rel=0&showinfo=0&html5=true   
 TROY, Ala. ( TROJANVISION ) — Daylight saving time came to an end this past weekend, with people across the country turning their clocks back one hour. 
 While some people welcomed the extra hour of sleep, others were not as enthusiastic about the change.
 “It’s felt really good to be able to have an extra hour in the morning of sunlight. Before this, the sun wasn’t rising until sometime after seven, so it’s been good to have some extra sunlight.”
 Although the time change provides more daylight in the morning, the earlier sunsets have become an adjustment for some students.
 HEALTH NEWS: How energy drinks affect students around campus 
 “In all honesty, I haven’t had too much of a change. The only thing is that it gets dark so soon. That’s a little iffy.”
 With classes, extracurricular activities and other responsibilities, students have different preferences when it comes to having more daylight in the morning or evening.
 Opinions also remain divided on whether daylight saving time should eventually be eliminated.
 “No, but I do think it needs to be either everybody adapts to it or nobody does.”
 One student believes the country needs a consistent approach to the time change.
 As students continue adjusting to the changing daylight hours, the debate over whether the country should continue changing its clocks twice a year remains.
 The next scheduled clock change will take place March 14, 2027, when clocks move forward one hour for daylight saving time.
